Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Activation of the MAPK Pathway in
Carcinoma Progression
Authors: Elena Vance, PhD, Marcus Thorne, MD, Alistair Chen, PhD
DOI: 10.1038/s41586-024-00101-x | PMID: 38291001 | PMCID: PMC10821001
Page 1 — Abstract & Introduction
The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) plays a central regulatory role in cellular proliferation and
oncogenic transformation. Binding of extracellular epidermal growth factor activates EGFR through receptor
dimerization. We investigate the sequential downstream signal transduction across cellular compartments.

Page 2 — Methods & Early Signaling
Phosphorylated EGFR recruits the adaptor protein GRB2 via its SH2 domain. Subsequently, GRB2 binds the
guanine nucleotide exchange factor SOS1 to form a stable binary signaling complex at the cell membrane.

Page 3 — Intermediate Cascade
Membrane-anchored SOS1 stimulates RAS by catalyzing GDP-GTP exchange. Active GTP-bound RAS directly
binds and activates RAF serine/threonine kinase, initiating the cytoplasmic kinase cascade.

Page 4 — Results & Kinase Phosphorylation
In our experimental assays, active RAF phosphorylates MEK at dual serine residues Ser217 and Ser221.
Activated MEK directly phosphorylates ERK to elicit full enzymatic activation of MAPK.

Page 5 — Discussion & Conclusions
Our findings demonstrate that active ERK translocates into the nucleus to stimulate transcription factors.
Consequently, EGFR signaling drives cellular proliferation through sequential MAPK activation. Inhibition of
